title: After a hospital stay
summary: Ask the right questions before leaving, and make the first days calm.
callNow: New trouble breathing, chest pain, or signs of a stroke
They is suddenly much more confused, very hard to wake, or can't keep fluids down

steps.title: Before leaving the hospital, ask
steps.text: What happened and what to watch for. Which medicines are new, changed or stopped. When the follow-up visit is and with whom. Whether home health care or equipment was ordered. Who to call with questions, day and night.

steps.title: Get it in writing
steps.text: Ask for the discharge papers and the updated medicine list. Take a photo of each page.

steps.title: Go over the medicines with the pharmacist
steps.text: Compare the new list with what's at home, so nothing old is taken by mistake.

steps.title: Make the first days calm
steps.text: Familiar room, a night light, a simple routine, water within reach, and the same short answers to the same questions.

steps.title: Expect more confusion for a while
steps.text: Many people with dementia are more confused after a hospital stay. Tell the doctor if it's getting worse instead of better, or if anything new appears.

then: Book the follow-up visit before you leave, or the next working day.
Ask family to cover the first few days; put tasks on the family board.
Do a quick safety check at home: clear paths, grab bars, lighting on the way to the bathroom.
dont: Don't leave without a written medicine list and a number to call.
Don't change doses on your own; ask the doctor or pharmacist.
